# edgeos_system_login_user_public_key (Resource)

An SSH public key of a login user (`system login user <user> authentication public-keys <name>`).

Keys are separate from `edgeos_system_login_user` so they can be added and rotated on their own; the user resource leaves `public-keys` alone. The user has to exist already: reference `edgeos_system_login_user` in `user` so Terraform creates it first. Destroying the key deletes only this key.

`key` is the base64 part of the key only, without the type in front or the comment at the end. For a line `ssh-ed25519 AAAAC3Nza... alice@laptop` set `type = "ssh-ed25519"`, `key = "AAAAC3Nza..."` and use the comment as `name`.

Before you set `disable_password_authentication` on `edgeos_service_ssh`, make sure the key works, or you lose SSH access to the router.

## Example Usage

```terraform
variable "alice_password" {
  type      = string
  sensitive = true
}

resource "edgeos_system_login_user" "alice" {
  name               = "alice"
  plaintext_password = var.alice_password
}

# From the public key line "ssh-ed25519 AAAAC3Nza... alice@laptop".
resource "edgeos_system_login_user_public_key" "alice_laptop" {
  user = edgeos_system_login_user.alice.name
  name = "alice@laptop"
  type = "ssh-ed25519"
  key  = "AAAAC3NzaC1lZDI1NTE5AAAAIAABAgMEBQYHCAkKCwwNDg8QERITFBUWFxgZGhscHR4f"
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `key` (String) The base64 encoded key, without type and comment.
- `name` (String) Name of the key, usually the comment of the key such as `alice@laptop`: letters, digits and `@`, `.`, `_`, `+`, `-`. Changing it creates a new key.
- `type` (String) Key type: `ssh-ed25519`, `ssh-rsa`, `ecdsa-sha2-nistp256`, `ecdsa-sha2-nistp384`, `ecdsa-sha2-nistp521` or `ssh-dss`. It has to match the type encoded in `key`.
- `user` (String) Login user the key belongs to. Changing it moves the key to another user.

### Optional

- `options` (String) Options in front of the key in `authorized_keys`, such as `no-agent-forwarding,no-port-forwarding`. EdgeOS cannot store double quotes, so options like `from="..."` are not possible.

### Read-Only

- `id` (String) `<user>:<name>`, for example `alice:alice@laptop`.

## Import

Import is supported using the following syntax:

In Terraform v1.5.0 and later, the [`import` block](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/language/import) can be used with the `id` attribute, for example:

```terraform
import {
  to = edgeos_system_login_user_public_key.alice_laptop
  id = "alice:alice@laptop"
}
```

The [`terraform import` command](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/commands/import) can be used, for example:

```shell
terraform import edgeos_system_login_user_public_key.example 'alice:alice@laptop'
```
